articles.title: Japan real wages rise for eighth straight month, backing case for BOJ hikes
articles.desc: The detail that matters most for the Bank of Japan is base pay. Regular wages holding steady near 4% points to durable wage growth rather than a bonus-driven spike, which is the kind of evidence policymakers want before tightening further. That supports the yen and front-end Japanese government bond
articles.content: The detail that matters most for the Bank of Japan is base pay. Regular wages holding steady near 4% points to durable wage growth rather than a bonus-driven spike, which is the kind of evidence policymakers want before tightening further. That supports the yen and front-end Japanese government bond yields at the margin, even as the headline real wage gain slowed. The risk to the real wage picture comes from prices. With the inflation measure used in the calculation only just above 2%, and Tokyo core inflation accelerating alongside elevated oil costs from the Middle East conflict, any pickup in the deflator would quickly erode real gains. That tension matches the Reuters Tankan earlier today, where service firms said inflation was squeezing household purchasing power despite rising pay. - Japanese workers are still getting ahead of inflation, and steady base pay growth gives the Bank of Japan another reason to keep raising rates. Summary: Japan's inflation-adjusted real wages rose 1.5% year on year in August, the eighth consecutive monthly increase, slowing from a revised 2% in July Total cash earnings rose close to 4% to about 311,000 yen, slower than a revised 4.3% in July Base salaries also grew close to 4%, matching July's pace, while overtime pay growth picked up to around 5% from 4.5% Special payments, mainly volatile one-off bonuses, were flat after rising around 5% in July The inflation measure used to calculate real wages held just above 2%, below about 3% a year earlier Japan's real wages rose for an eighth straight month in August, government data showed on Wednesday, extending a run of gains that supports the case for further interest rate increases by the Bank of Japan. Inflation-adjusted pay rose 1.5% from a year earlier, slower than the revised 2% increase recorded in July. Average nominal wages, measured as total cash earnings, grew close to 4% to about 311,000 yen, down from a revised 4.3% rise the previous month. The slowdown in headline earnings came largely from bonuses. Special payments, which are mostly one-off and tend to swing sharply from month to month, showed no growth in August after rising around 5% in July. Underlying pay was steadier. Base salaries, or regular pay, rose close to 4%, the same pace as in July, while overtime pay growth accelerated to around 5% from 4.5%, a sign that firms are still working staff harder. The inflation measure the labour ministry uses to calculate real wages held at just above 2% in August, unchanged from July and well below the roughly 3% rate a year earlier. That lower deflator has been a key reason real pay has stayed positive. The data adds to evidence that Japan is moving toward the sustained cycle of rising wages and prices the central bank has sought for years. The BOJ raised its policy rate to 1.25% in September, and Tokyo core inflation accelerated in September at its fastest pace in 10 months, strengthening the argument for further tightening. Not all signals point the same way. A Reuters business survey published earlier on Wednesday showed sentiment among Japanese service companies falling sharply, with retailers and food producers saying inflation was eroding household purchasing power. Bank of Japan board member Ayano Sato, who opposed September's hike, also said this week that she favours raising rates gradually, without a pre-set pace. Whether real wage gains can be sustained will depend on prices. With oil costs elevated by the Middle East conflict, a faster rise in inflation would narrow the margin by which pay is outpacing living costs. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

Navitas Closes Acquisition of Claros, Advancing AI Infrastructure with Grid-to-xPU Power Delivery
articles.desc: Completes Navitas’ high-power portfolio with Claros’ IVR technology, enabling vertical and embedded architectures and providing last step in power delivery to the core
articles.content: Navitas Closes Acquisition of Claros, Advancing AI Navitas Closes Acquisition of Claros, Advancing AI Infrastructure with Grid-to-xPU Power Delivery Completes Navitas’ high-power portfolio with Claros’ IVR technology, enabling vertical and embedded architectures and providing last step in power delivery to the core Navitas to host webinar ‘Breaking the AI Infrastructure Power Wall: From Grid-to-xPU’, unveiling Claros’ technology and differentiation TORRANCE, Calif., Oct. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Navitas Semiconductor (Nasdaq: NVTS) (Navitas or “the Company”), a leader in next-generation power semiconductors and power delivery solutions, pioneering GaN, high-voltage and ultra-high-voltage SiC, and IVR technologies, today announced the closing of its previously announced acquisition of Claros, Inc. (Claros), a power management solutions company developing integrated voltage regulator (IVR) technology for next-generation AI data centers, providing the last step to powering the xPU. The completed transaction extends Navitas’ AI infrastructure portfolio from the grid to the xPU, bringing industry-leading IVR capabilities. Claros™ IVR integrates power transistors, digital control, inductors and capacitors into a single IVR technology stack to enable next-generation Vertical Power Delivery (VPD) and Embedded Power Delivery (EPD) architectures. Its Packaged Integrated Voltage Regulator (pIVR) and Embedded Integrated Voltage Regulator (eIVR) products, based off the same Claros IVR technology stack, move power conversion closer to the xPU and deliver higher efficiency, faster transient response and greater power density, while the modular PowerArray™ architecture scales power delivery to meet the rapidly increasing demands of next-generation processors at the center of modern AI systems. Combined with Navitas’ GaN and high-voltage and ultra-high-voltage SiC technologies that enable the new 800V DC architecture, the Company is “breaking the AI infrastructure power wall” by addressing the efficiency, power density and performance bottlenecks emerging as AI data centers and xPUs demand dramatically more power. “Closing this acquisition is a defining step in the Navitas 2.0 transformation and our strategy to power AI infrastructure from grid-to-xPU,” said Chris Allexandre, President and CEO of Navitas. “With power now the bottleneck for AI, increases in power delivery and efficiency are the key enablers of more compute output. The future of AI depends on delivering thousands of amps to increasingly power-hungry processors with unprecedented speed and precision, in addition to re-redefining the racks with higher power centralized systems and higher density architectures. This ‘power wall’ has restricted next-generation xPUs in megawatt-scale server racks from achieving the next wave of AI performance. Navitas 2.0 brings together GaN, high-voltage and ultra-high-voltage SiC, and now IVR technologies to break the power wall and address power conversion across the complete grid-to-xPU architecture. “Additionally, this combination doubles our serviceable addressable market (SAM), deepens our engagement with hyperscalers and AI power platform providers, and strengthens our capabilities and leadership in power delivery for AI infrastructure. As AI power demand accelerates, we are uniquely positioned to deliver greater value for our customers, while driving sustainable long-term growth.” Navitas expects the acquisition to more than double the Company’s identified 2030 SAM to over $8 billion, adding at least $3.5 billion from the rapidly growing VPD and IVR markets. Combined with Navitas’ existing $3.5 billion SAM for GaN and HV/UHV SiC and approximately $1 billion from new JFET technology, the transaction significantly expands Navitas’ opportunity across the complete grid-to-xPU power chain. Webinar Presentation | Breaking the AI Infrastructure Power Wall: From Grid-to-xPU Chris Allexandre - Navitas President and CEO Llew Vaughan-Edmunds - Navi

articles.title: Topology-dependent FRET efficiency in living cells via N-C swapping of fluorescent protein fusions
articles.desc: Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) is a physicochemical phenomenon involving non-radiative energy transfer between donor and acceptor fluorophores. While FRET efficiency primarily depends on the proximity between fluorophores, additional factors substantially influence the efficiency in living
articles.content: Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) is a physicochemical phenomenon involving non-radiative energy transfer between donor and acceptor fluorophores. While FRET efficiency primarily depends on the proximity between fluorophores, additional factors substantially influence the efficiency in living cells. However, how non-distance factors modulate live-cell FRET efficiency remains poorly understood. Here, we report the significant role of N- and C-terminal topology in determining live-cell FRET efficiency, independent of fluorophore proximity, donor variants, and subcellular compartment. Using acceptor photobleaching and sensitized emission measurements in living cells, we found that FRET efficiencies of mCherry-EGFP or mCherry-EYFP (acceptor-donor) were significantly higher than those of EGFP-mCherry or EYFP-mCherry (donor-acceptor), respectively. FRET efficiencies were higher with EYFP than with EGFP as the donor. These efficiencies were comparable between the nucleus and cytoplasm. AlphaFold2-based structural modeling suggested similar proximity between donor and acceptor fluorophores despite structurally heterogeneous and loosely constrained geometries. In contrast, ensemble FRET simulations suggested that dynamic conformational sampling amplifies the apparent asymmetry between donor-acceptor and acceptor-donor configurations observed in live-cell FRET measurements. Collectively, these results demonstrate that topological arrangement, rather than static structural geometry alone, plays a significant role in FRET efficiency in living cells, providing molecular implications for the design of intramolecular FRET-based biosensors.

articles.title: Infinix Launches Smart 20 HD with 120Hz Display and IP64 Rating in India
articles.desc: Infinix Smart 20 HD launches in India at Rs 10,999 with a 120Hz punch-hole screen, 5000mAh battery, dual speakers, and IP64 splash protection.
articles.content: Infinix Launches Smart 20 HD with 120Hz Display and IP64 Rating in India Infinix officially introduced its budget-focused smartphone, the Infinix Smart 20 HD, in the Indian market on October 6, 2026. The device targets everyday users who need solid media playback, long battery life, and durable hardware at an affordable price. Priced starting at Rs 10,999 inclusive of offers, the phone features a 6.67-inch HD+ punch-hole screen with a 120Hz refresh rate, an octa-core Unisoc processor, and an IP64 rating for dust and splash protection. Sales begin across Flipkart and local retail stores with six-month no-cost EMI schemes. 6.67-inch HD+ punch-hole screen with 120Hz refresh rate and 700 nits peak brightness Unisoc T7250 octa-core processor with 48-month fluency testing 5000mAh battery with 15W charging support and 10W charger in the box Dual speakers featuring up to 300 percent Ultra Volume mode and DTS audio IP64 dust and water splash resistance with touch support for greasy fingers Ultra Link offline communication up to 200 meters via Bluetooth Price starts at Rs 10,999 for the 3GB RAM and 64GB storage model Hardware and Display Features Infinix built the Smart 20 an 8.25mm slim chassis that weighs light in hand despite packing a large 5000mAh battery. The front features a 6.67-inch HD+ display running at a resolution of 720 x 1600 pixels. The 120Hz refresh rate keeps UI animations fluid, while the 700 nits high brightness mode helps screen clarity under direct sunlight. The phone comes in three color finishes, namely Sunlike Orange, Silver Dancer, and Night Pulse. Performance and Battery Life Under the hood, the device runs on a 12nm Unisoc T7250 octa-core chipset. The processor pairs two performance Cortex-A75 cores clocked at 1.8GHz with six power-friendly Cortex-A55 cores running at 1.6GHz. Infinix pairs the chip with 3GB RAM, which users can expand by up to 3GB extra using virtual memory management. Internal storage stands at 64GB, expandable via a dedicated microSD card slot. . The 5000mAh battery handles a full day of mixed use on a single charge. While the phone accepts charging speeds up to 15W, Infinix bundles a standard 10W power brick inside the retail packaging. Multimedia and Connectivity Tools For multimedia lovers, the phone packs dual stereo speakers supporting DTS audio and an Ultra Volume feature that boosts sound levels up to 300 percent for noisy areas. It features an 8MP rear camera alongside an 8MP selfie shooter, supporting 2K video recording at 30 frames per second, Super Night mode, and dual-video mode. The phone brings a dedicated Ultra Link feature that allows local , voice notes, calls, and file transfers over Bluetooth within a 200-meter range without any active cellular network or SIM card. For standard voice calls, three noise reduction options, including Pure Voice voiceprint filtering, help cut out ambient crowd sounds. Q1. What is the official price of the Infinix Smart 20 HD in India? A1. The phone starts at Rs 10,999 including promotional discounts, available with six-month no-cost EMI options. Q2. Does the Infinix Smart 20 HD support fast charging? A2. The handset supports up to 15W charging speed, but it includes a 10W charger inside the retail box. Q3. What is the screen refresh rate on this smartphone? A3. The 6.67-inch punch-hole HD+ display supports a refresh rate of up to 120Hz. Q4. Is the Infinix Smart 20 HD waterproof? A4. It carries an IP64 rating, which protects against fine dust and direct water splashes, but it is not submersible. Q5. How does the Ultra Link feature work? A5. Ultra Link relies on Bluetooth connectivity to let users chat, share images, and make calls within a 200-meter distance without a SIM card or mobile data. articles.title: Lucid cut production 38% in the third quarter as deliveries slipped 7%
articles.desc: The EV maker produced 2,954 vehicles from July through September, its lowest quarterly output since early 2025
articles.content: Lucid Q3 2026 production and delivery results Lucid cut production 38% in the third quarter as deliveries slipped 7% The EV maker produced 2,954 vehicles from July through September, its lowest quarterly output since early 2025 on Monday that third-quarter output came in at 2,954 vehicles while 3,806 were handed over to customers, with management intentionally throttling the production line to burn through a stockpile of finished cars sitting in inventory. Output was 38% below the 4,774 units assembled in the prior quarter, according to . Deliveries dropped 6.7% from the 4,078 vehicles the company handed over in the third quarter of 2025, according to . For the first time this year, deliveries exceeded production — by 852 units — as the company drew down existing vehicle inventory rather than building new cars to meet demand. The results reflect CEO Silvio Napoli's "operating reset," an effort targeting $1.4 billion in cash flow improvements in 2026, the company said. Breaking that target down, the company is looking to recover $600 million to $800 million by selling off vehicle inventory, trim another $500 million through reduced capital investment, and shave roughly $200 million from its operating expense base. The company added that its Gravity SUV had seen demand "continued to regain momentum" but stopped short of disclosing any model-level sales figures. The third quarter marked the first complete three-month stretch in which 's Arizona facility ran on a single shift after previously operating two. That shift elimination, announced in June, was part of the same operating reset and was consistent with the sequential production decline, the company said. cut approximately 18% of its U.S. workforce in June when Napoli took over as CEO, eliminating the second shift at its AMP-1 plant in Casa Grande, Arizona, and removing the chief operating officer role. That restructuring followed an earlier 12% headcount reduction in February. A seat defect that halted Gravity SUV shipments in February caused more than $200 million in revenue impairment during the first quarter and forced to withdraw its full-year production guidance of 25,000 to 27,000 vehicles. has produced 13,228 vehicles and delivered 10,852, according to Electrek. stock closed up less than 1% on Monday at $4.17 and was little changed in after-hours trading. The stock is down more than 60% this year. will report full third-quarter financial results, including net income and cash flow, on November 9, the company said. articles.title: An AI app is now writing first-time acne prescriptions in Utah without a doctor
articles.desc: Nolla Health's Nolla Derm app received state approval to issue initial prescriptions autonomously, with physician oversight built in at each stage
articles.content: Nolla Health AI app issues acne prescriptions in Utah without a doctor An AI app is now writing first-time acne prescriptions in Utah without a doctor Nolla Health's Nolla Derm app received state approval to issue initial prescriptions autonomously, with physician oversight built in at each stage that its Nolla Derm app has become the first AI system in the United States authorized to issue initial prescriptions, starting with acne medication in Utah. The company said Utah residents 18 and older can sign up for the program at $4.99 a month. The app works by asking patients to complete a 10-to-15-minute intake questionnaire and a face scan. According to , the AI examines the patient's skin, produces a numerical acne severity score, and identifies an appropriate treatment from a set of eight pre-approved topical options. Prescriptions are delivered to a pharmacy or the patient's home. If the AI cannot select a treatment with confidence, the patient is referred to a licensed physician instead. The program operates in three stages with declining levels of direct physician involvement. During the first stage, which covers the initial 100 patients enrolled, every prescription the AI produces must pass through physician review before being sent to a pharmacy. In the second stage, which encompasses the following 400 patients, the AI sends prescriptions straight to pharmacies while a physician looks them over after the fact on a weekly basis. Once the program moves past those initial 500 patients, physician oversight shifts to a monthly audit covering no fewer than one in ten prescriptions issued, the company said. Nolla Health received approval through the Utah Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy, a division of the Utah Department of Commerce that authorizes companies to test AI products under relaxed regulations. Under the pilot, prescriptions carry a clinician's name without a human professional writing them, according to Bloomberg. The program is set to run for one year, with the option to renew for two more years at the state's discretion. The company said licensed clinicians agree with the AI's treatment recommendations in more than 96% of real-world cases, with disagreements limited to minor adjustments such as topical medication strength. The system cannot generate open-ended prescriptions and is restricted to pre-approved topical treatments. Patients with severe acne, pregnancy, or other conditions outside the pilot's scope are referred to a physician. According to Bloomberg, Zachary Boyd, director of Utah's Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy, said the state carved out a "narrow exception" for Nolla Health, setting aside the state statute that ordinarily restricts prescribing authority to licensed physicians. Boyd added that the office does not anticipate the same controversy that followed an earlier AI prescription pilot in the state because Nolla Health's program is limited to acne medication and is the first company to engage with the Utah Medical Licensing Board before receiving authorization. The company said the Nolla Derm app has been downloaded by more than 175,000 people across 44 states. Chief Executive Luis Wenus said in a statement that the goal is to help patients receive care "in minutes instead of long waits or going without care altogether." articles.title: Morgan Stanley says Nvidia and Broadcom are shielded from data-center power crunch
articles.desc: Secondary chip suppliers — including makers of memory, optical, and power-management components — face the greater risk of order disruptions
articles.content: Morgan Stanley: Nvidia, Broadcom shielded from data-center power crunch Morgan Stanley says Nvidia and Broadcom are shielded from data-center power crunch Secondary chip suppliers — including makers of memory, optical, and power-management components — face the greater risk of order disruptions have meaningful protection against the deteriorating U.S. data-center power situation, while warning that a slowdown in AI buildout could hit suppliers of memory, optical, and related chip components with order disruptions, according to In a report last month, the bank put the net power shortfall facing U.S. data-center developers at 34% through 2028 — around 32 gigawatts — even when factoring in behind-the-meter generation and fuel cells. said it does not see those bottlenecks putting 's 2027 forecasts at risk, according to Reuters. credited the two chipmakers' ability to monitor where their products are being installed, pursue growth across multiple geographies, and work closely with data-center operators and power-sector partners as a structural cushion that smaller, lower-tier suppliers simply do not have, according to Reuters. That flexibility could allow to redirect chips toward data-center projects that have secured power if another facility is delayed, while suppliers tied to the delayed project have fewer options, according to Should deployment timelines slip, buyers may delay or walk away from orders altogether, and identified memory, optics, power-management, and analog components as the product categories carrying the heaviest inventory risk in that scenario, according to Reuters. 's competitive edge sharpens precisely when power is scarce, because customers under electricity pressure prioritize the most computationally efficient hardware available, according to Benzinga. CEO Jensen Huang has echoed that framing, noting that before any computing gear goes into a facility, developers must first line up real estate, electricity, and the building structure itself — a sequence he said routinely runs two to three years, according to Benzinga. The power crunch is part of a broader strain on U.S. electricity infrastructure driven by gigawatt-scale AI data centers coming online this year 's AI training chips can draw 120 to 140 kilowatts per rack, and the transmission infrastructure needed to power new facilities takes five to ten years to plan and energize — far longer than the 18 to 36 months it takes to build a data center. has also flagged mounting constraints on the U.S. data-center buildout but expects limited near-term impact from political opposition. 's analysis identifies labor, power, and political challenges as the combined pressure points, according to the outlet. The essential business news, delivered fresh every morning.
